title: Semantics of a two-step register addition
statement:
Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program with $m$ registers, oracle family $O$, input $x$, and space bound $B$. Let $k,y,p$ be registers with $k
e y$, $k
e p$, and $p
e y$, and suppose the instruction at state $\mathrm{test}$ compares registers $k$ and $y$, branching to $\mathrm{ex}$ on equality and to $i_1$ otherwise; the instructions at $i_1$ and $i_2$ each increment $p$ and proceed respectively to $i_2$ and $i_3$, and the instruction at $i_3$ increments $k$ and returns to $\mathrm{test}$. If the current register values $v(r)$ are all at most $B$, $v(k)\le v(y)$, and $v(p)+2(v(y)-v(k))\le B$, then for any proposition $P$, if the configuration at $\mathrm{ex}$ with $p$ replaced by $v(p)+2(v(y)-v(k))$ and $k$ replaced by $v(y)$ has terminating nondeterministic semantics with space guard $B$ and acceptance equivalent to $P$, the configuration at $\mathrm{test}$ with the original register values has the same semantics.
hypotheses_covered: $k,y,p$ are registers and are pairwise distinct

The instruction at $i_1$ increments $p$ and proceeds to $i_2$
The instruction at $i_2$ increments $p$ and proceeds to $i_3$
The instruction at $i_3$ increments $k$ and returns to $\mathrm{test}$
Every current register value is at most $B$
The stated terminal configuration has terminating semantics under the register bound $B$ and acceptance equivalent to $P$
